I will keep this year simple and grow the crop system I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I would not spread myself into several crops. In Quzhou, wheat-maize double cropping is the main pattern, with more than 80% of fields using it, and the local high-yield work in the county is built around that system ([Scientific Reports](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep41587), [China Agricultural University Quzhou Station](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html)). At 65, with primary-school education, I would choose a familiar, mechanized, lower-risk grain rotation that I can manage steadily. I would plan on 10 mu because that is a workable scale for me. For wheat, I would use an improved variety, plough after straw return, give it most of the irrigation, and keep fertilizer at a moderate level instead of chasing demonstration-field input levels. For maize, I would use hybrid seed, sow directly after wheat harvest with no-tillage, rely mostly on summer rainfall, and only irrigate when the field really needs it. My fertilizer rates follow the local Quzhou/Hebei direction of moderate nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium, especially for summer maize ([Hebei summer maize fertilization guidance](https://www.zynylm.com/zhibao/2019/0222/3071.html)). My yield targets are steady farmer targets, not the county’s best demonstration results.
